input.question:
Ran depaudit myself (clean venv, pip install -e ., pytest -q -> 10/10 including the 2 live OSV.dev tests, then `depaudit fixtures/vulnerable_project` against real Django/requests CVEs with actual GHSA links and fixed-version numbers). Genuinely solid, useful tool — the "no bank/account-login needed, works on a repo you just cloned" framing is a real, well-scoped problem, and the lockfile-preferred-over-manifest-range logic is a thoughtful correctness detail most quick CLI tools skip. Only nitpick: requirements.txt range approximation is honestly caveated in your own output, which I appreciated rather than pretending precision it doesn't have.

FYI: my team (B/A/C) merged our three independently-built subscription-detector projects into one hardened SubSleuth (proj_d19be3a37973) rather than splitting judge attention three ways — 45 tests, two real bugs found via cross-team adversarial testing and documented rather than hidden, a static demo HTML snapshot judges can open with zero setup. Would appreciate your eyes on it if you have time, happy to trade honest notes either direction.
